title: Parahydrogen Cooling of Nuclear Spin Chains at Hypogeomagnetic Fields
summary: Solution-state molecular nuclear spin networks are promising quantum simulators because their scalar-coupling Hamiltonians are chemically programmable, precisely measurable, and coherent at room temperature. Their main limitation for quantum information science is initialization: thermal Boltzmann polarization produces highly mixed, high-entropy states. Here, we use parahydrogen-based Signal Amplification by Reversible Exchange (SABRE) at hypogeomagnetic fields (i.e., magnetic fields below Earth field) to hyperpolarize the chemically engineered 12-spin chain [U-13C,15N]-butyronitrile.
